value.body: Indian Railways recruits non-officer staff through 21 Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs). After Class 12, the two main openings are the undergraduate-level NTPC posts — Commercial cum Ticket Clerk, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Junior Clerk cum Typist and Trains Clerk — and Level-1 posts (formerly Group D), such as track maintainer and helper, which need Class 10 or an ITI certificate.

items.label: Recruitment boards
items.note: You apply to one RRB / zone per notice

value.title: How you get in
value.body: NTPC undergraduate posts need Class 12; typing posts also need a typing skill test. Level-1 posts need Class 10, ITI or equivalent. Selection is one or two computer-based tests, then a typing test (for typist posts) or a physical efficiency test (for Level-1), followed by document verification and a medical exam. Age limits and relaxations are stated in each notice.

value.title: At a glance
items: Application volumes are very large — Level-1 drives have drawn over a crore applicants.
Medical standards differ by post; check them before applying.
RRB exams now follow an annual calendar, but results and joining can take more than a year.
Posts carry central-government pay scales and railway benefits, with postings anywhere in the chosen zone.
